q: The ε-net theorem (from combinatorics/learning theory) states that for a set system (X,𝒮) with VC dimension d, a random sample of size O((d log(1/ε))/ε) is an ε-net with probability ≥ 3/4. This is related to information theory by:
opts: Sample complexity bounds use entropy of the hypothesis class: log|𝒮_n| ≤ O(d log n) (Sauer-Shelah)
exp: Sauer-Shelah lemma: |𝒮_n| ≤ O(n^d) for VC dimension d. The entropy of the hypothesis class over n points is O(d log n) bits, directly controlling the sample complexity via uniform convergence bounds. The log factor in ε-nets comes from the entropy of the class.
